source_text: Aemulari aliquem irritare etiam est et provocare. In Deuteronomio: Ipsi in zelum adduxerunt me in non Deo; et ego in zelum adducam eos. Apostolus: An aemulamur Dominum? Deus noster Deus zelans. Qui peccat Deum zelantem in zelum incitat.
pass_a_gloss: To envy someone is also to irritate and provoke. In Deuteronomy: They brought me to jealousy with a non-god; and I will bring them to jealousy. The Apostle: Are we provoking the Lord to jealousy? Our God is a jealous God. Who sins stirs the jealous God to jealousy.
pass_b_english: Here aemulari means to provoke jealousy. Deuteronomy: [[They made me jealous with what is no god; I will make them jealous >> Bible:Deuteronomy 32:21]]. Paul asks [[Are we provoking the Lord to jealousy? >> Bible:1 Corinthians 10:22]]. [[The Lord your God is a jealous God >> Bible:Exodus 20:5]] — sin stokes that zeal.
